Start one scenario of an analysis project version

Source: R/initialize_project.R
initialize_project.Rd

initialize_project() sets up one simulation of one scenario of a project version, and sources the functions folder of that version. It MUST be the first call in every vNN_run.R.

Usage

initialize_project(version, home, data_raw, env = .GlobalEnv)

Arguments

version

The version, written as "v" and two digits, for example "v01".

home

The project folder. It holds <version>_run.R and <version>_functions/.

data_raw

The folder of the real raw data. It MUST exist when the scenario is "real". pbn does not read it for any other scenario.

env

The environment that the functions folder is sourced into.

Value

Invisibly, a list with version, home, scenario, sim, sims, results and data_raw. results is the results folder and data_raw is the data folder of the run.

Details

_cfg.R in <version>_functions/ MUST set CFG$scenarios, a data.frame with these columns:

  • scenario: unique names that match ^[a-z0-9_]+$. One name MUST be "real".

  • sims: the number of simulations of the scenario, a whole number of 1 or more.

The scenario and the simulation come from the first of these that gives them. pbn reads no environment variables.

  1. The trailing command-line arguments scenario=<name> and sim=<k>. run_scenarios() gives both. When only one of them is there, the other one is "real" or 1.

  2. The choice of use_scenario(), for a person who steps through the script by hand.

  3. The scenario "real" and the simulation 1.

The choice of use_scenario() lasts for the R session.

In an interactive R session, initialize_project() prints one line, for example pbn: scenario null, simulation 2 of 3 (fake). (fake) is there for each scenario other than "real".

initialize_project() does these steps in this order:

  1. It calls org::initialize_project() with results set to <home>/<version>_results, results_subfolder set to the scenario, folders_to_be_sourced set to <version>_functions, and max_loc_per_file set to 1000.

  2. It reads CFG$scenarios. The results folder is <version>_results/<scenario>/ when the scenario has 1 simulation, and <version>_results/<scenario>/sim_<kkkk>/ otherwise. <kkkk> is the simulation with four digits. org::project$results_today is set to this folder.

  3. It calls set.seed(sim). It also calls set.seed(sim) before step 1, so random work while org sources the functions folder depends on sim only.

  4. For "real", the data folder is data_raw. For any other scenario, the data folder is data/ in the results folder. initialize_project() deletes it, creates it empty, and calls fake_<scenario>(dir) with its path. The project MUST define fake_<scenario>() in <version>_functions/.

  5. It computes the md5 of each file directly in the data folder. save_results() stores these values as manifest$data_md5, so a file that the run writes later is not in the list.

initialize_project() stops in these cases:

  • scenario= or sim= is given more than once.

  • sim= is not a whole number of 1 or more.

  • The scenario is not in CFG$scenarios, or sim is more than its sims.

  • fake_<scenario>() is missing.

When it stops, it deletes each empty results folder that the call created. The state of the run is then empty, so save_results() and end_if_fake_scenario() stop until a call succeeds. The choice of use_scenario() stays. It never creates a folder with today's date.

See also

Other project setup: end_if_fake_scenario(), run_scenarios(), use_scenario()

Examples

home <- file.path(tempdir(), "pbn_initialize_example")
dir.create(file.path(home, "v01_functions"), recursive = TRUE)
dir.create(file.path(home, "data"))
writeLines(
  c(
    "CFG <- list(",
    "  scenarios = data.frame(scenario = c('real', 'null'), sims = c(1, 3))",
    ")",
    "fake_null <- function(dir) {",
    "  utils::write.csv(data.frame(x = rnorm(5)), file.path(dir, 'd.csv'))",
    "}"
  ),
  file.path(home, "v01_functions", "_cfg.R")
)

utils::write.csv(data.frame(x = 1:5), file.path(home, "data", "d.csv"))

env <- new.env()
p <- pbn::initialize_project(
  version = "v01",
  home = home,
  data_raw = file.path(home, "data"),
  env = env
)
#> You are NOT sourcing into .GlobalEnv. All functions will be sourced into an environment that is returned from this function.
#> Sourcing all code inside /tmp/RtmpoLbHrA/pbn_initialize_example/v01_functions into 
p$scenario
#> [1] "real"
p$results
#> [1] "/tmp/RtmpoLbHrA/pbn_initialize_example/v01_results/real"
list.files(p$data_raw)
#> [1] "d.csv"

unlink(home, recursive = TRUE)
